text: It’s 1780 in Paris, and the heavy spring rains are saturating the earth.
ipa: /ˈɪts 1780 ɪn pˈɛɹɪs ənd ðə hˈɛvi spɹˈɪŋ ɹˈeɪnz ˈɑɹ sˈætʃɚˌeɪtɪŋ ðə ˈɝθ/
vi: Năm 1780 tại Paris, những cơn mưa xuân nặng hạt đang thấm đẫm mặt đất.

text: In a home near the center of town, a basement wall collapses under the pressure, releasing
ipa: /ɪn ə hˈoʊm nˈɪɹ ðə sˈɛntɚ ˈʌv tˈaʊn ə bˈeɪsmənt wˈɔl kəlˈæpsɪz ˈʌndɚ ðə pɹˈɛʃɚ ɹilˈisɪŋ/
vi: Trong một ngôi nhà gần trung tâm thị trấn, một bức tường tầng hầm bị sập dưới áp lực, giải phóng

text: a flood of decomposing corpses— remains from the neighboring Cemetery of the Innocents.
ipa: /ə flˈʌd ˈʌv dˌikəmpˈoʊzɪŋ kˈɔɹpsəz ɹɪmˈeɪnz fɹˈʌm ðə nˈeɪbɚɪŋ sˈɛmətˌɛɹi ˈʌv ðə ˈɪnəsənts/
vi: một dòng xác chết đang phân hủy— tàn tích từ Nghĩa trang Vô tội lân cận.

text: Rumors spread that everyone in the house got sick due to bad air emanating
ipa: /ɹˈumɚz spɹˈɛd ðˈæt ˈɛvɹiwˌʌn ɪn ðə hˈaʊs ɡˈɑt sˈɪk dˈu tˈu bˈæd ˈɛɹ ˈɛmənˌeɪtɪŋ/
vi: Tin đồn lan truyền rằng mọi người trong nhà đều bị ốm do không khí bốc mùi khó chịu

text: from the decaying flesh.
ipa: /fɹˈʌm ðə dɪkˈeɪɪŋ flˈɛʃ/
vi: từ thịt thối rữa.

text: With the overcrowded cemetery housing generations of dead Parisians, there was a growing worry
ipa: /wˈɪð ðə ˈoʊvɚkɹˌaʊdɪd sˈɛmətˌɛɹi hˈaʊzɪŋ dʒˌɛnɚˈeɪʃənz ˈʌv dˈɛd pɚˈɪsiənz ðˈɛɹ wˈɑz ə ɡɹˈoʊɪŋ wˈɝi/
vi: Với nghĩa trang quá tải, nơi an nghỉ của nhiều thế hệ người Paris đã khuất, nỗi lo ngại ngày càng tăng

text: that the entire city was in grave danger of falling ill.
ipa: /ðˈæt ðə ɪntˈaɪɚ sˈɪti wˈɑz ɪn ɡɹˈeɪv dˈeɪndʒɚ ˈʌv fˈɑlɪŋ ˈɪl/
vi: toàn bộ thành phố đang gặp nguy hiểm nghiêm trọng về việc bị bệnh.

text: For centuries, Parisians had buried their dead in the Innocents, the city’s largest cemetery.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ sˈɛntʃɚiz pɚˈɪsiənz hˈæd bˈɛɹid ðˈɛɹ dˈɛd ɪn ðə ˈɪnəsənts ðə citys lˈɑɹdʒəst sˈɛmətˌɛɹi/
vi: Trong nhiều thế kỷ, người dân Paris đã chôn cất người chết của họ tại Innocents, nghĩa trang lớn nhất thành phố.

text: While cemeteries across Europe were originally placed outside of urban areas, in the 9th century
ipa: /wˈaɪl sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz əkɹˈɔs jˈʊɹəp wˈɝ ɚˈɪdʒənəli plˈeɪst ˈaʊtsˈaɪd ˈʌv ˈɝbən ˈɛɹiəz ɪn ðə 9th sˈɛntʃɚi/
vi: Trong khi các nghĩa trang trên khắp châu Âu ban đầu được đặt bên ngoài khu vực thành thị, vào thế kỷ thứ 9

text: the Church began allowing burials directly on its grounds.
ipa: /ðə tʃˈɝtʃ bɪɡˈæn əlˈaʊɪŋ bˈɛɹiəlz dɚˈɛktli ˈɑn ˈɪts ɡɹˈaʊndz/
vi: Nhà thờ bắt đầu cho phép chôn cất trực tiếp trên khuôn viên của mình.

text: As these urban parish cemeteries filled, some churches started creating bone chapels, like the Sedlec Ossuary
ipa: /ˈæz ðˈiz ˈɝbən pˈæɹɪʃ sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz fˈɪld sˈʌm tʃˈɝtʃɪz stˈɑɹtɪd kɹiˈeɪtɪŋ bˈoʊn chapels lˈaɪk ðə sedlec ossuary/
vi: Khi các nghĩa trang giáo xứ đô thị này đầy lên, một số nhà thờ bắt đầu tạo ra các nhà nguyện xương, như Sedlec Ossuary

text: in the Czech Republic, to make room for new burials.
ipa: /ɪn ðə tʃˈɛk ɹipˈʌblək tˈu mˈeɪk ɹˈum fˈɔɹ nˈu bˈɛɹiəlz/
vi: ở Cộng hòa Séc, để dành chỗ cho những ngôi mộ mới.

text: By the 18th century, public opinion on urban cemeteries shifted,
ipa: /bˈaɪ ðə 18th sˈɛntʃɚi pˈʌblɪk əpˈɪnjən ˈɑn ˈɝbən sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz ʃˈɪftɪd/
vi: Vào thế kỷ 18, dư luận về các nghĩa trang đô thị đã thay đổi,

text: as Enlightenment thinkers and physicians promoted new scientific ideas that linked hygiene to health.
ipa: /ˈæz ˌɛnlˈaɪtənmənt θˈɪŋkɚz ənd fəzˈɪʃənz pɹəmˈoʊtɪd nˈu sˌaɪəntˈɪfɪk aɪdˈiəz ðˈæt lˈɪŋkt hˈaɪdʒˌin tˈu hˈɛlθ/
vi: khi các nhà tư tưởng và y bác sĩ Thời Khai Sáng thúc đẩy các ý tưởng khoa học mới liên kết vệ sinh với sức khỏe.

text: They didn't yet understand the concept of germs, believing instead
ipa: /ðˈeɪ dˈɪdənt jˈɛt ˌʌndɚstˈænd ðə kˈɑnsɛpt ˈʌv dʒˈɝmz bɪlˈivɪŋ ˌɪnstˈɛd/
vi: Họ vẫn chưa hiểu khái niệm về mầm bệnh, thay vào đó tin rằng

text: that disease spread through “miasma,” or bad air.
ipa: /ðˈæt dɪzˈiz spɹˈɛd θɹˈu miˈæzmə ˈɔɹ bˈæd ˈɛɹ/
vi: căn bệnh đó lây lan qua "miasma", hay không khí độc hại.

text: Consequently, overcrowded cemeteries spewing cadaverous odors were cast as public health threats.
ipa: /kˈɑnsəkwəntli ˈoʊvɚkɹˌaʊdɪd sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz spjˈuɪŋ cadaverous ˈoʊdɚz wˈɝ kˈæst ˈæz pˈʌblɪk hˈɛlθ θɹˈɛts/
vi: Do đó, các nghĩa trang quá tải với mùi tử thi nồng nặc bị coi là mối đe dọa sức khỏe cộng đồng.

text: Even after the Innocents and other cemeteries closed in the early 1780s, residents continued to worry
ipa: /ˈivɪn ˈæftɚ ðə ˈɪnəsənts ənd ˈʌðɚ sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz klˈoʊzd ɪn ðə ˈɝli 1780s ɹˈɛzɪdənts kəntˈɪnjud tˈu wˈɝi/
vi: Ngay cả sau khi các nghĩa trang Innocents và các nghĩa trang khác đóng cửa vào đầu những năm 1780, cư dân vẫn tiếp tục lo lắng

text: about the foul smells and petitioned the government for a long-term solution.
ipa: /əbˈaʊt ðə fˈaʊl smˈɛlz ənd pətˈɪʃənd ðə ɡˈʌvɚmənt fˈɔɹ ə lˈɔŋtˌɝm səlˈuʃən/
vi: về mùi hôi và đã kiến nghị chính phủ giải pháp lâu dài.

text: But where could they move the remains of the millions of Parisians?
ipa: /bˈʌt wˈɛɹ kˈʊd ðˈeɪ mˈuv ðə ɹɪmˈeɪnz ˈʌv ðə mˈɪljənz ˈʌv pɚˈɪsiənz/
vi: Nhưng họ có thể di dời hài cốt của hàng triệu người dân Paris đến đâu?

text: The vast abandoned network of quarries beneath the city offered a logical solution.
ipa: /ðə vˈæst əbˈændənd nˈɛtwˌɝk ˈʌv kwˈɔɹiz bɪnˈiθ ðə sˈɪti ˈɔfɚd ə lˈɑdʒɪkəl səlˈuʃən/
vi: Mạng lưới các mỏ đá bỏ hoang rộng lớn bên dưới thành phố đã đưa ra một giải pháp hợp lý.

text: Dating back to Roman times, the mines had provided the limestone and plaster to build Paris.
ipa: /dˈeɪtɪŋ bˈæk tˈu ɹˈoʊmən tˈaɪmz ðə mˈaɪnz hˈæd pɹəvˈaɪdɪd ðə lˈaɪmstˌoʊn ənd plˈæstɚ tˈu bˈɪld pˈɛɹɪs/
vi: Có niên đại từ thời La Mã, các mỏ đã cung cấp đá vôi và thạch cao để xây dựng Paris.

text: But by the 18th century, they had begun collapsing under the city’s weight, creating deadly sinkholes.
ipa: /bˈʌt bˈaɪ ðə 18th sˈɛntʃɚi ðˈeɪ hˈæd bɪɡˈʌn kəlˈæpsɪŋ ˈʌndɚ ðə citys wˈeɪt kɹiˈeɪtɪŋ dˈɛdli sinkholes/

text: So in 1777, King Louis XVI established a team of engineers to survey
ipa: /sˈoʊ ɪn 1777 kˈɪŋ lˈuɪs xvi ɪstˈæblɪʃt ə tˈim ˈʌv ˈɛndʒənˈɪɹz tˈu sɚvˈeɪ/

text: and reinforce the area.
ipa: /ənd ɹˌiɪnfˈɔɹs ðə ˈɛɹiə/

text: And in 1785, Charles-Axel Guillaumot, the Inspector General of Quarries, was tasked with turning sections
ipa: /ənd ɪn 1785 charlesaxel guillaumot ðə ˌɪnspˈɛktɚ dʒˈɛnɚəl ˈʌv kwˈɔɹiz wˈɑz tˈæskt wˈɪð tˈɝnɪŋ sˈɛkʃənz/

text: of the unused tunnels into a massive crypt.
ipa: /ˈʌv ðə ənjˈuzd tˈʌnəlz ˈɪntu ə mˈæsɪv kɹˈɪpt/

text: The Catholic Church initially resisted, as it stood to lose income from burials
ipa: /ðə kˈæθlɪk tʃˈɝtʃ ˌɪnˈɪʃəli ɹɪzˈɪstɪd ˈæz ˈɪt stˈʊd tˈu lˈuz ��ɪnkˌʌm fɹˈʌm bˈɛɹiəlz/

text: and cemetery maintenance fees, but public health concerns prevailed.
ipa: /ənd sˈɛmətˌɛɹi mˈeɪntənəns fˈiz bˈʌt pˈʌblɪk hˈɛlθ kənsˈɝnz pɹɪvˈeɪld/

text: The transfer of human remains was done mostly at night, to avoid upsetting passersby
ipa: /ðə tɹænsfˈɝ ˈʌv hjˈumən ɹɪmˈeɪnz wˈɑz dˈʌn mˈoʊstli ˈæt nˈaɪt tˈu əvˈɔɪd əpsˈɛtɪŋ pˈæsɚzbi/

text: and to limit public exposure to the miasma.
ipa: /ənd tˈu lˈɪmət pˈʌblɪk ɪkspˈoʊʒɚ tˈu ðə miˈæzmə/

text: Millions of anonymous bones were dug up by hand, carted across Paris,
ipa: /mˈɪljənz ˈʌv ənˈɑnəməs bˈoʊnz wˈɝ dˈʌɡ ˈʌp bˈaɪ hˈænd kˈɑɹtɪd əkɹˈɔs pˈɛɹɪs/

text: and dumped unceremoniously in the Catacombs.
ipa: /ənd dˈʌmpt ˌʌnsˌɛɹəmˈoʊniəsli ɪn ðə kˈætəkˌoʊmz/

text: It was a distinctly modern project, focused on efficiency rather than memorialization.
ipa: /ˈɪt wˈɑz ə dɪstˈɪŋktli mˈɑdɚn pɹˈɑdʒɛkt fˈoʊkəst ˈɑn ɪfˈɪʃənsi ɹˈæðɚ ðˈæn memorialization/

text: The Cemetery of the Innocents was the largest source,
ipa: /ðə sˈɛmətˌɛɹi ˈʌv ðə ˈɪnəsənts wˈɑz ðə lˈɑɹdʒəst sˈɔɹs/

text: though bones were soon brought from cemeteries throughout the city.
ipa: /ðˈoʊ bˈoʊnz wˈɝ sˈun bɹˈɔt fɹˈʌm sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz θɹuˈaʊt ðə sˈɪti/

text: The French Revolution temporarily stalled relocation efforts, though the Catacombs did offer a space
ipa: /ðə fɹˈɛntʃ ɹˌɛvəlˈuʃən tˌɛmpɚˈɛɹəli stˈɔld ɹˌilˈoʊkˈeɪʃən ˈɛfɚts ðˈoʊ ðə kˈætəkˌoʊmz dˈɪd ˈɔfɚ ə spˈeɪs/

text: where inconvenient bodies could disappear.
ipa: /wˈɛɹ ˌɪnkənvˈinjənt bˈɑdiz kˈʊd dˌɪsəpˈɪɹ/

text: Some of the over 1,000 prisoners executed in the Revolution’s September Massacres of 1792
ipa: /sˈʌm ˈʌv ðə ˈoʊvɚ 1000 pɹˈɪzənɚz ˈɛksəkjˌutɪd ɪn ðə ɹˌɛvəlˈuʃənz sɛptˈɛmbɚ mˈæsɪkɚz ˈʌv 1792/

text: were hastily cast there.
ipa: /wˈɝ hˈeɪstəli kˈæst ðˈɛɹ/

text: However, the Catacombs weren’t generally used for new burials.
ipa: /hˌaʊˈɛvɚ ðə kˈætəkˌoʊmz werent dʒˈɛnɚəli jˈuzd fˈɔɹ nˈu bˈɛɹiəlz/

text: Instead, the newly dead were interred in garden cemeteries established, once again, on the city’s outskirts.
ipa: /ˌɪnstˈɛd ðə nˈuli dˈɛd wˈɝ ˌɪntˈɝd ɪn ɡˈɑɹdən sˈɛmətˌɛɹiz ɪstˈæblɪʃt wˈʌns əɡˈɛn ˈɑn ðə citys ˈaʊtskˌɝts/

text: By the end of the Revolution, the relocation project had sprung back to life.
ipa: /bˈaɪ ðə ˈɛnd ˈʌv ðə ɹˌɛvəlˈuʃən ðə ɹˌilˈoʊkˈeɪʃən pɹˈɑdʒɛkt hˈæd spɹˈʌŋ bˈæk tˈu lˈaɪf/

text: And in 1809, Napoleon Bonaparte, aware of the unifying power of monuments, ordered
ipa: /ənd ɪn 1809 nəpˈoʊliən bˈoʊnəpˌɑɹt əwˈɛɹ ˈʌv ðə jˈunəfˌaɪɪŋ pˈaʊɚ ˈʌv mˈɑnjəmənts ˈɔɹdɚd/

text: that a small section of the chaotic space be curated and open to the public.
ipa: /ðˈæt ə smˈɔl sˈɛkʃən ˈʌv ðə keɪˈɑtɪk spˈeɪs bˈi kjʊɹˈeɪtɪd ənd ˈoʊpən tˈu ðə pˈʌblɪk/

text: Piles of bones were pushed to the sides, facades of skulls
ipa: /pˈaɪlz ˈʌv bˈoʊnz wˈɝ pˈʊʃt tˈu ðə sˈaɪdz fəsˈɑdz ˈʌv skˈʌlz/

text: and femurs were artfully arranged, and quotes about the fleeting nature of life
ipa: /ənd femurs wˈɝ ˈɑɹtfəli ɚˈeɪndʒd ənd kwˈoʊts əbˈaʊt ðə flˈitɪŋ nˈeɪtʃɚ ˈʌv lˈaɪf/

text: were hung on the walls.
ipa: /wˈɝ hˈʌŋ ˈɑn ðə wˈɔlz/

text: The rest of the Catacombs— housing the remains of an estimated 6 million Parisians—
ipa: /ðə ɹˈɛst ˈʌv ðə kˈætəkˌoʊmz hˈaʊzɪŋ ðə ɹɪmˈeɪnz ˈʌv ˈæn ˈɛstəmˌeɪtəd 6 mˈɪljən pɚˈɪsiənz/

text: was, and largely remains, untouched.
ipa: /wˈɑz ənd lˈɑɹdʒli ɹɪmˈeɪnz əntˈʌtʃt/

text: After its beautification, the Catacombs became a hugely popular tourist destination.
ipa: /ˈæftɚ ˈɪts beautification ðə kˈætəkˌoʊmz bɪkˈeɪm ə hjˈudʒli pˈɑpjəlɚ tˈʊɹəst dˌɛstənˈeɪʃən/

text: While signs indicated the cemetery where the bones were moved from, the remains themselves were anonymous—
ipa: /wˈaɪl sˈaɪnz ˈɪndəkˌeɪtəd ðə sˈɛmətˌɛɹi wˈɛɹ ðə bˈoʊnz wˈɝ mˈuvd fɹˈʌm ðə ɹɪmˈeɪnz ðɛmsˈɛlvz wˈɝ ənˈɑnəməs/

text: aristocrats lay next to laborers, raiders next to defenders, the young next to their elders.
ipa: /ɚˈɪstəkɹˌæts lˈeɪ nˈɛkst tˈu lˈeɪbɚɚz ɹˈeɪdɚz nˈɛkst tˈu dɪfˈɛndɚz ðə jˈʌŋ nˈɛkst tˈu ðˈɛɹ ˈɛldɚz/

text: And so, the site became a symbol
ipa: /ənd sˈoʊ ðə sˈaɪt bɪkˈeɪm ə sˈɪmbəl/

text: of what one 19th-century photographer called the “confused equality of death.” Sources vary,
ipa: /ˈʌv wˈʌt wˈʌn 19thcentury fətˈɑɡɹəfɚ kˈɔld ðə kənfjˈuzd ɪkwˈɑləti ˈʌv dˈɛθ sˈɔɹsəz vˈɛɹi/

text: but some say the last remains were moved as recently as the 1930s.
ipa: /bˈʌt sˈʌm sˈeɪ ðə lˈæst ɹɪmˈeɪnz wˈɝ mˈuvd ˈæz ɹˈisəntli ˈæz ðə 1930s/

text: Today, people from around the world continue to visit the Catacombs, finding, amidst its caverns,
ipa: /tədˈeɪ pˈipəl fɹˈʌm ɚˈaʊnd ðə wˈɝld kəntˈɪnju tˈu vˈɪzɪt ðə kˈætəkˌoʊmz fˈaɪndɪŋ əmˈɪdst ˈɪts kˈævɚnz/

text: a haunting reminder of our shared, inevitable future.
ipa: /ə hˈɔntɪŋ ɹimˈaɪndɚ ˈʌv ˈaʊɚ ʃˈɛɹd ˌɪnˈɛvətəbəl fjˈutʃɚ/
